title: Certificates of Deposit: Grace Add-On Room and the Savings Balance Behind a Top-Up
content:
A grace top-up within the bank's Certificates of Deposit has to sit inside two limits: what the grace period still allows to be added, and what the owner's savings can supply. This page defines both and how a top-up is held against them.

## Room left in the grace period

The room is the tier's grace maximum less what has been paid in during the present grace period. What has been paid in is measured as every grace-period add-on deposit whose posting date lies in the month leading up to the date under review. That one-month look-back takes in the whole of the current grace period and nothing from any earlier one, because successive grace periods on a certificate are at least six months apart.

## The savings balance

The other limit is the current balance in the owner's open savings or money market account at PCB from which the money is drawn.

## Holding the top-up against both

Neither limit may be exceeded: the top-up has to fit within what the grace period still admits and within that savings balance. If it exceeds either, no top-up is written at all; the top-up is never reduced so as to squeeze under a limit.

## Cases (hypothetical figures: grace maximum assumed at USD 200000.00 purely for illustration; date under review 9 October)

| Grace add-ons posted 9 September to 9 October | Room left | Savings balance | Top-up | Written? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | USD 200000.00 | USD 12000.00 | USD 3779.55 | Yes |
| USD 199000.00 | USD 1000.00 | USD 12000.00 | USD 3779.55 | No; it exceeds the room |
| none | USD 200000.00 | USD 2500.00 | USD 3779.55 | No; it exceeds the savings balance, and it is not cut to USD 2500.00 |
